scope.description: Exact published-record refresh for MetOcean Telematics using official product, Canadian and U.S. procurement, counterparty and independently documented field-use evidence.

source.title: USCG iSLDMB call 70Z03826FD0000023
source.locator: Award profile, obligation, description and period
source.summary: Official award data records a USD 470,005 iSLDMB call for USCG search-and-rescue operations from 2026-08-12 through 2027-09-01.

leads.evidenceLocator: USCG and DND awards; MetOcean product documents; Frontiers and Petrobras PABLO evidence; Iridium, Brazilian Navy and FLANQ counterparty records
followUpQuestions: Which NiKA/PAMS and iSLDMB configurations have been delivered and accepted under the cited awards, and what non-sensitive test results can be shared?
Which personnel, facility, cybersecurity and data-handling controls apply to each defence configuration beyond Controlled Goods registration?
What unit capacity, lead time, quality-certificate scope and Canadian workshare apply to NiKA, iSLDMB, PABLO, STREAM and MASS orders?
For the selected mission, which sensing, satellite, software and third-party components are included, and where are the integration and data-return boundaries?
reviewWarnings: The three USCG iSLDMB calls establish obligations, not disclosed unit count, delivery, acceptance or operational performance.
The DND NiKA/PAMS award establishes a contract but does not publish delivered quantity, acceptance result or measured performance.
PABLO's independently documented Santos Basin use is environmental deployment evidence and must not be converted into defence validation.
NiKA transmits acoustic and position data after surfacing; public sources do not support continuous underwater satellite connectivity.
The UK Ministry of Defence MASS award is confirmed, but Royal Navy commissioning, acceptance, measured performance and operational use remain unverified.
KSSL and Indian Ministry of Defence records do not independently name MetOcean or NiKA, so that claimed contract linkage remains excluded.
ZeroUSV and third-party coverage identify the Oceanus12 satellite stack but do not independently identify MetOcean's integration role.
No independent current ISO certificate number, scope, sites or expiry was recovered for MetOcean's quality claim.
Bracer FIPS status conflicts between the current page and the 2023 sheet, and no NIST certificate or module number was found.
STREAM1 cold-temperature claims conflict between the current product advisory and the version 7 specification.
Controlled Goods registration is confirmed, but personnel, facility, cybersecurity, data-residency and product-accreditation scope remains undisclosed.
The CAD 15.142 million Shared Services Canada contract is an as-required ceiling and does not establish realized spend or use by every named partner organization.
Public sources do not disclose product-level production capacity, backlog, unit pricing, domestic workshare or standard delivery lead time.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Confirmed MetOcean's current Dartmouth operating footprint, product families, public contact route and owner-controlled manufacturing claims.
Resolved NiKA depth, hydrophone, endurance and surfaced Certus data-return architecture while retaining vendor-performance limits.
Confirmed legal recipient, business number and Dartmouth location through the federal contribution record; private ownership remains undisclosed.
Checked current Canadian trademark and historical patent trails; no new active-patent claim changed the dossier decision.
Resolved the USCG parent BPA and three iSLDMB calls plus the DND NiKA/PAMS award without inferring unit count, delivery or acceptance.
Confirmed Controlled Goods registration through 2031-01-28 while leaving clearance, cyber-accreditation and configuration scope unresolved.
Reviewed current Canadian contract history and retained distinct government buyer and contribution records without summing amendments as revenue.
Resolved independent PABLO deployment, Brazilian Navy iSLDMB sustainment, Canadian Coast Guard integration support and FLANQ counterparty evidence.
Checked English and French Canadian procurement surfaces; no separate canonical French company site was found.

Final certification and counterparty falsification found Bracer FIPS and STREAM1 temperature conflicts, but no current ISO certificate or durable counterparty proof for KSSL or ZeroUSV; the MASS award was confirmed while commissioning remains unknown.
